class.name: PhysicsServer4D
class.brief_description: Physics server for managing 4D physics simulation and objects.
class.description: PhysicsServer4D is the glue that brings together physics bodies and areas in the scene and prepares them for physics simulation by a physics engine. [PhysicsBody4D] and [Area4D] nodes will register themselves with the physics server. Each frame, the physics server will call the physics engine to simulate the scene. The details of how the scene is simulated are up to the physics engine. [b]Note:[/b] Godot's 2D and 3D physics servers are data-driven and duplicate the relevant data from the scene nodes into the physics engine's data structures. For simplicity, PhysicsServer4D is node-driven, meaning that the data provided to physics engines is the actual scene nodes themselves. This will continue to be the case unless the additional complexity of data-driven physics is justified by benchmarks and the needs of actual projects.

method.name: get_area_nodes
method.description: Gets an array of all area nodes in the scene. This is useful for physics engines to check for overlaps with areas.

method.name: get_physics_body_nodes
method.description: Gets an array of all physics body nodes in the scene. This is useful for physics engines to check for overlaps with bodies.

method.name: get_physics_engine_names
method.description: Returns a list of all [PhysicsEngine4D] names that have been registered with the physics server using [method register_physics_engine].

method.name: raycast_physics_objects
method.description: Performs a raycast in the scene using the provided [RaycastParameters4D] and returns a Dictionary with the results. See [RaycastParameters4D] for details on how to configure the raycast. The Dictionary may contain various keys depending on what was hit. If the function errors, the returned Dictionary will be empty: [code]{}[/code]. If no hit was found, the returned Dictionary will be [code]{"hit": false}[/code]. If a hit was found, the Dictionary will contain all of the keys provided by the responsible [method Node4D.raycast_intersects_local] and [method Shape4D.raycast_intersects] functions, including [code]"hit"[/code], [code]"distance"[/code], [code]"normal"[/code], [code]"point"[/code], and more. See the documentation for those functions for details on what keys may be present in the returned Dictionary. The [code]"distance"[/code], [code]"normal"[/code], and [code]"point"[/code] keys are local to the shape, exactly as the shape's raycast function returned them. Since this PhysicsServer4D function accepts global inputs, it also calculates global outputs, which are provided in separate [code]"global_"[/code] prefixed keys in the returned Dictionary: - [code]"global_distance"[/code]: The distance from the ray's origin to the hit point in global space. - [code]"global_normal"[/code]: The normal of the hit surface in global space. Only present if the shape-local [code]"normal"[/code] key is also present. - [code]"global_point"[/code]: The hit point's position in global space. Only present if the shape-local [code]"point"[/code] key is also present. Additionally, if a hit was found, the returned Dictionary will have the following keys added to it by this function: - [code]"body"[/code]: The [CollisionObject4D] node that was hit, which may be a [PhysicsBody4D] or an [Area4D]. - [code]"shape"[/code]: The [CollisionShape4D] node that was hit, a member of the [code]"body"[/code] node (usually a descendant of it).

method.name: register_physics_engine
method.description: Register a physics engine extending [PhysicsEngine4D] with the physics server, making it available to be used.

method.name: unregister_physics_engine
method.description: Unregister a physics engine with the physics server by name.

members.member: Whether the physics server is active. If set to [code]false[/code], the physics server will not simulate the scene. By default, this is [code]true[/code] when running projects, and [code]false[/code] when in the editor.
The name of the current physics engine being used. If only one physics engine is registered, this will be set to that engine's name automatically.
